title: Smooth strict-local closed fibre as a strict henselization
statement:
Let $f:V\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\bar s=f\bar v$. Put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$, $B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar v}$, as geometric strict local rings [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the canonical map of strict local rings [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Write $\mathfrak m_A$ for the maximal ideal and $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-residue-field], with its canonical embedding into $\Omega$. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the canonical closed geometric point, $W=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $Z=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The point $(\bar v,a)$ factors through a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$; let $z$ be its image. The scheme $Z$ is smooth over $\kappa$, and there are canonical isomorphisms
$$B/\mathfrak m_A B\simeq\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar z}\simeq(\mathcal O_{Z,z})^{\mathrm{sh}},$$
where the last strict henselization [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] uses the separable closure of $\kappa(z)$ inside $\Omega$. These identify the quotient map from $B$ with the functorial map on strict local rings induced by the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow W$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the canonical identification of the strict local rings of $W$ and $V$. On every affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum] $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset W$, the closed subscheme $Z$ is given by $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\mathfrak m_A D)$. The ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and its strict henselization are Noetherian regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. No regularity or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is required.

proof.text: Apply the smooth strict-local base-model theorem. It supplies the local base ring, the evaluation-kernel equality, smoothness of W over Spec A, and the comparisons theta:H_W to H and beta:B to H with their structural and evaluation equations. No Noetherian hypothesis is used.

The kernel equality identifies A/ker(eval) with the residue field, so it is a field. Factor evaluation by kerLift. Its composite with the quotient map is evaluation. The base-model geometric point and this factorization therefore define the geometric point zbar of Z by the pullback universal property. Smooth base change makes Z smooth over this field. The base change of the quotient spectrum is a closed immersion.
Apply the generic quotient-base-change affine model to every affine chart j:Spec D to W. It gives exactly D/m_A D and the projection equation, including nilpotents.

Set eW=beta inverse after theta. The evaluation equations show that eW preserves evaluation. The spectrum equation in the base model identifies Spec eW with the inverse of the strict-local projection, giving the structural equation over V. Its composite with the structural map to Spec A lies over f and preserves evaluation; uniqueness of the canonical pointed strict-local morphism identifies it with strictHenselizationMap f v. Full faithfulness of Spec gives the A-action equation. Transport along zbar followed by the closed-fibre projection equals the base-model point.

Apply the generic strict-local quotient-base-change theorem to Z inside W. The A-action equation shows that eW maps the extended ideal in H_W exactly to m_A B. Ideal.quotientEquiv transports the quotient; compose its inverse with the generic comparison. Its formula on quotient representatives proves the required equation with the canonical quotient map.

The geometric strict-local stalk presentation supplies the exact final colimit presentation and its two equations. The existing smooth-scheme-over-field regularity theorem gives regularity of the ordinary stalk. In particular it is Noetherian. The presentation is definitionally a witness of IsStrictHenselization, so the strict-henselization regularity equivalence gives regularity of H_Z. Return these witnesses together with the quotient comparisons.
